_about: M5 spike results measured so far (2026-10-03). Raw outputs and the scripts that produced them are in docs/v2/research/m5-spikes/. Everything here was measured on a local desktop with onnxruntime 1.29.0 (the production pin); nothing here was measured on Fly hardware yet. Added 2026-11-05: S6_fly_timing and S6_fly_rss, measured on Fly (window W1, sin, one-off machines of image registry.fly.io/semigraph-stg:w1fp32 built with EMBEDDER_VARIANT=fp32 KEEP_UNPATCHED=1; the machines were destroyed after).

S6_local_query_embedding.model: Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B, 8-bit MatMulNBits (block 128, symmetric), model_q8.onnx as built by scripts/build_onnx_embedder.py
S6_local_query_embedding.input: constant 17-token instruction prefix + a question; median 32.5 tokens in the timing set (6 realistic questions)

shipped_model_no_accuracy_level.profile: 98% of the time is MatMulNBits (1.177 s of 1.199 s per call, 196 nodes); tokenization 0.0002 s; fetching one output instead of all 57 changes nothing (1.218 vs 1.229 s)
shipped_model_no_accuracy_level.reading: a fixed floor of about 1 s per call even for 4 tokens, consistent with every weight being dequantized to fp32 on each call: the profile shows 98% of the time in MatMulNBits, and ORT's CPU source falls back to dequantize-then-float-GEMM for 8-bit weights unless accuracy_level=4 (docs/v2/research/m5-facts-cloud-2026-10-03.md section E). The builder never sets the accuracy_level attribute.
shipped_model_no_accuracy_level.source_file: docs/v2/research/m5-spikes/embed_profile_shipped_venv_baseline.json (threads 1 and 2; the 4-thread value is from embed_profile_local.json, dev env)

patched_accuracy_level_4.how: attribute accuracy_level=4 set on the 196 MatMulNBits nodes of the same weights (no re-quantization), scratch copy
patched_accuracy_level_4.long_passages: 257 tokens 2.739 s -> 2.482 s: document embedding for uploads is barely affected

retrieval_parity_vs_shipped_model.CORRECTION: 2026-10-03: the first version of this block (53 questions, top-1 identical 0.962, top-8 identical 0.83, top-8 mean overlap 0.9788) was measured with the wrong query prompt ('Query: ' with a trailing space) on the 53 examples only, and is withdrawn. Production's QUERY_PROMPT ends '\nQuery:' and the pre-registered check uses the 60 benchmark+example questions. Figures below are from scripts/verify_embedder_parity.py on the production prompt.

retrieval_parity_vs_shipped_model.result: FAIL: the pre-registered top-1 gate is not met. Held pending the owner's decision (docs/v2/M5_DECISIONS.md section 1.4 item 12, section 7 decision 14).

derived_load_note: with the patch, one question embed is about 0.31 s of a desktop core (about 0.37 s assuming a Fly core 19% slower; UNVERIFIED). At 2.6 live asks/s that is about 1.0 core-s/s when every embed is cold and about 0.33 core-s/s warm, versus 3.9 and 1.3 before. A shared-cpu-2x sustains 12.5% of one core (Fly docs), so it still cannot meet a 70%-of-sustained CPU criterion at the gate load; the gate is proven on a performance-class staging fleet instead.

S6_fly_rss.reading: PASS by 14,872 kB (0.6% of the limit). The fp32 weights are private anonymous memory on Linux (+1.26 GB vs q8), not a shared file mapping. M4's total budget was 2.8 GB with the upload-parse child capped at 1 GiB (measured child peak 41 MB).

W0_fresh_machine_throttle.window: W0, 2026-11-05 17:21Z-18:51Z, Fly sin, a NEW shared-cpu-2x 4 GB machine (flyctl machine run; the harness deploy path gave a performance-1x because fly.tools.toml's [[vm]] overrode --vm-size: harness bug, fixed with W1b)
W0_fresh_machine_throttle.report: Throttled from second 115: the throughput stayed below 90% of the baseline 6,599,376 iterations/s; it sustained 1,114,317 iterations/s, 17% of the baseline. An idle pulse was back to 90% of the baseline after 60 s of rest.
W0_fresh_machine_throttle.reading: Fly's documented 5 s initial burst balance was NOT what we saw: a fresh shared-cpu-2x ran one core at full speed for about 115 s, then held about 17% of it; 60 s of rest gave a short burst back. For the live site (ops.ps1 start creates a new machine): an embed takes about 1.2 s (q8) or 0.33 s (fp32) while the burst lasts and about 10 s (q8) or 2.8 s (fp32) once it is gone (W1).
